dedupe_keys.name: saint petersburg ambulance dispatching to heart attack centres with coupled game theory and discrete event simulation

description: This case study models how ambulances in a large city choose the destination hospital for patients with acute coronary syndrome who need percutaneous coronary intervention, and how the differing strategies of hospitals affect the whole system. The authors, researchers at ITMO University, the Almazov National Medical Research Centre, the University of Amsterdam and Utrecht University, coupled a game-theoretic model, in which hospitals are players in a non-cooperative game, with a discrete event simulation of patient delivery and treatment, and published the work in a journal article that is free to read online on the publisher's site. The approach was tested on a simplified one-dimensional model, a coupled two-dimensional model and a real-world case with data from Saint Petersburg, Russia. Coverage is one city. Caveats: the case covers one condition and one city, and the hospital data are not public. The study found that representing hospitals' diverse behaviour made the simulated system match real global indicators, such as the mortality rate, better than models that ignore it. Simulation uses: a coupling pattern for multi-agent hospital and ambulance dispatch simulation. Related records: the NYC EMS response time study (case_study-nyc-ems-response-time-inequities-2010-2020) and the Liberia national EMS study (case_study-liberia-national-ems-first-22-months) cover ambulance services elsewhere.
